title: Case Study: Japan and Haiti
welcome_lead: Two earthquakes, two very different outcomes. Compare Japan 2011 and Haiti 2010 to see why preparation matters.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography case study comparing Japan 2011 and Haiti 2010 earthquakes.

walkthroughs.body_html: A magnitude 9.0 quake struck off Japan's coast, triggering a deadly tsunami. Japan's strict building codes saved many lives, but the tsunami killed around 15,000 people.
Haiti's quake measured 7.0 — smaller than Japan's — but killed over 200,000 people. Weak buildings and poor emergency services made things worse.
HICs like Japan can afford earthquake-proof buildings, drills and warnings. LICs like Haiti often cannot, so people suffer more.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between outsourcing and offshoring?
options: Outsourcing means moving to another country and offshoring means hiring contractors.

Outsourcing means contracting work to another company; offshoring means relocating work to another country. A firm can outsource without offshoring, or offshore without outsourcing (in-house overseas).
Outsourcing and offshoring are the same thing.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.

mcqs.q: Why does oceanic crust subduct beneath continental crust?
options: Continental crust subducts because it is thicker and heavier.
Oceanic crust is denser (basaltic) than continental crust (granitic), so when they collide the denser oceanic plate sinks into the mantle, forming a trench and volcanic arc.
Oceanic crust subducts because the ocean pushes it down with its weight.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
